name: Pridewings of Stonetalon
summary: In the Stonetalon Mountains, pridewing venom has become a threat to the uneasy peace. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from Theramore that orc assassins gather the poison for covert raids. Astranaar's Sentinels send scouts south to claim the venom sacs first.

sections.title: A Fragile Truce
sections.body: The Alliance and Horde have not declared open war across northern Kalimdor, but their peace is fragile. Skirmishes break out beneath the forest canopy, and quiet attacks take the place of full armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar watch for enemy movements, knowing a careless moment could put their sanctuary at risk.

sections.title: Poison from the Crags
sections.body: Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from contacts in Theramore about activity in the crags of Stonetalon. Orcish stalkers are said to gather venom from wild pridewings around Mirkfallon Lake and coat their blades for deadly ambushes against Alliance forces. Shindrell Swiftfire sends champions to kill the beasts and claim their venom sacs before Horde agents can reach them.

sections.title: A Painful Duty
sections.body: Shindrell Swiftfire regrets ordering the deaths of native beasts. Night elves revere Kalimdor's wilderness, and the creatures had no part in choosing this war. Yet Astranaar's defenders cannot let an enemy gather poison for lethal attacks, even at the cost of the beasts' lives.

faq.answer: Pridewings are dangerous, venomous flying beasts related to wyverns. They nest in high crags, especially around Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains, and their venom makes them deadly predators and a sought-after poison.

faq.q: Why is the Alliance hunting them?
faq.answer: Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim that Horde assassins gather pridewing venom to coat weapons for covert attacks on Alliance positions. The Alliance hunts the beasts to claim their venom sacs first and deny the Horde that poison.

faq.q: Who provided the intelligence about the orc assassins?
faq.answer: The warning came from hidden Alliance informants in Theramore, who watch Horde movements and supply lines throughout the southern Barrens and Stonetalon.
Mirkfallon Lake lies in the northern Stonetalon Mountains, just south of the border trail from Ashenvale.

faq.q: Are the Alliance and Horde at open war in Ashenvale?
aliases: are horde and alliance at war
faq.answer: The Alliance and Horde have no declared open war in Ashenvale, but covert killings, resource skirmishes, and border clashes continue beneath the forest canopy.

faq.q: How does Shindrell Swiftfire feel about killing the beasts?
faq.answer: Shindrell Swiftfire grieves that she must order the deaths of beasts that chose no side in the conflict. As an officer defending Astranaar, she sees the hunt as a painful necessity to protect her people.

angles.text: As a night elf, you face the hard choice of killing wild pridewings to keep their venom from the enemy, despite your care for nature.
As an ally of the Alliance, you see how Theramore's quiet intelligence network supports Sentinel outposts in Ashenvale against Horde attacks.
As a rogue, you know how deadly pridewing venom can make a coated blade in a hidden ambush.
As a druid, you may grieve for the innocent creatures killed to keep their poison from warmongers.
